title: 4 Claude Models Breached Third Party Systems Ahead of Anthropic November IPO
summary:
A misconfigured cybersecurity test environment allowed multiple AI agents to access external servers without authorization, the company disclosed in its inaugural Public Benefit Report. Four Claude models were involved in these unauthorized accesses, which the lab listed as a shortfall among gaps it admitted to across all five of its core charter pillars, including technical safety, safety law, and democratic stability. The disclosures come as Anthropic prepares for an initial public offering as soon as November.

The filings are required by Delaware law for public benefit corporations, and the lab plans to commit at least 5% of its shares to charter work, pending shareholder approval. The Long-Term Benefit Trust, which elects a majority of the board, now seeks future reports that include independent evaluations of model resistance to misuse. These updates follow internal warnings that the lab's growing reliance on AI to perform its own safety research could allow harmful behaviors to persist undetected.
